description: What if the data you engineer could stop fraud before it happens - and protect millions of AWS customers worldwide? The Payments and Fraud Data Platform team within AWS Payments & Fraud is the backbone of one of the most critical missions at AWS: ensuring every transaction is safe, every suspension is justified, and every customer experience is seamless. We process petabytes of data daily, powering the ML models, rule engines, and real-time reporting systems that allow us to detect bad actors. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who is passionate about building large-scale data systems, thrives in ambiguity, and wants to work at the intersection of big data, machine learning, non-payment and fraud prevention. Power ML & Rules Engines - Deliver high-quality, timely datasets that fuel non payment and fraud detection ML models and business rule engines, directly impacting fraud prevention and non-payment suspension accuracy. Develop Real-Time Dashboards & Insights - Build rich, interactive dashboards using Grafana and internal tooling that provide real-time visibility into fraud trends, pipeline health, data quality metrics, and operational KPIs. Curate a Living Data Dictionary - Design and maintain a comprehensive, searchable data catalog and dictionary that provides rich metadata, lineage, and documentation - improving discoverability and self-service analytics across the organization. Champion Data Quality at Scale - Implement automated data validation, anomaly detection, and reconciliation frameworks that ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency across the entire data lifecycle. Secure & Govern Sensitive Data - Implement encryption, fine-grained access controls, audit trails, and compliance frameworks to protect highly sensitive payments and fraud data. Monitor, Optimize, Repeat - Build observability into everything , proactive alerting, pipeline performance tracking, SLA monitoring, and intelligent auto-remediation to ensure five-nines data reliability. About the team The AWS Payments & Fraud Prevention team protects AWS and its customers from fraud, abuse, and account compromise at global scale. We build highly scalable, batch and near real-time systems that ingest billions of signals daily, process petabytes of data, and make timed decisions to stop bad actors from account registration through the entire customer lifecycle. Our platform is built on a modern, cloud-native architecture designed for petabyte-class batch processing. Our stack includes Amazon MWAA orchestrates workflows, while EMR and Fargate handle scalable data processing. Amazon Redshift powers our data warehouse, complemented by an Apache Iceberg lakehouse for open table format flexibility. DynamoDB and OpenSearch drives search and analytics, and Amazon Bedrock serves as our AI/ML foundation. title: Software Development Engineer,  Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management
description: Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management (LIM) Operations Tooling team builds the products that run the Leo network day to day. Our tools are used by the Network Operations Center, Call Leaders, and service teams across Networking, Commerce, and Satellite Operations to see the health of the network, catch problems before customers do, coordinate fast when something goes wrong, and automate the work that slows operators down. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and tools that power network operations and incident management for Amazon Leo. - Build proactive health capabilities, including anomaly and trend detection, early warning features, and proactive investigation workflows that help operators act before customers are affected. - Build alarm correlation and deduplication systems so responders see one problem instead of hundreds of alerts. - Build NOC dashboards and operator workflows that bring health, customer impact, affected components, and ongoing events into one view. - Build self-service tooling that lets service teams onboard and manage their own health signals, alarms, and runbooks. - Automate runbook steps, data collection, and repetitive operational tasks so operators spend their time on judgment, not mechanics. - Integrate with observability, telemetry, ticketing, paging, and communication systems across Amazon Leo, including the network observability platform. - Apply automation, machine learning, and generative AI to triage, event summarization, timeline drafting, and correlation where it measurably improves outcomes. - Design systems that stay available when the network they serve is degraded, since operators need these tools most during an outage. - Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support. - Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software. A day in the life You might start the day with feedback from the NOC on a dashboard you shipped last week and fix a workflow that slowed operators down during an overnight event. Midday, you could be designing a correlation service that groups alarms from many services into a single event, or building the escalation engine that pages the right leader when an event has been open too long. In the afternoon you might pair with the product manager on a self-service onboarding flow, review code, and prototype an AI-drafted event summary for Call Leaders. Your work shows up every time an issue is caught earlier, resolved faster, or never happens at all. About the team The Leo NOC and LIM Operations Tooling team builds the operational products that keep a global space and terrestrial telecom network healthy and its operations efficient.
